title: Oscar and the Autopsy
premise: True-crime podcaster Orsen Okonkwo built his reputation closing cases no one else could, so when a confession letter for the forty-year-old Hollowmere drowning arrives postmarked the day after the victim's funeral, he takes it personally — especially since the letter names him. Following a ledger of funeral dates and flower orders hidden in the town's church records, Orsen discovers the confession is a dying message from the killer's daughter, who inherited both her father's guilt and his unfinished business. As she dies, she begs him to finish what her love for a Hollowmere heir could not: expose the truth without destroying the family that sheltered her. In the end, Orsen broadcasts the confession, closes the case, and chooses belonging over the solitary duty that has defined him.
about_author: I. M. Whitlock is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent two decades cataloguing small-town deaths and the secrets they keep. They write mysteries about inheritance, guilt, and the letters people leave behind.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Orsen Okonkwo, POV. A confession letter for the 1984 Hollowmere drowning arrives the day after the victim's sister's funeral, naming Orsen by name and daring him to close the case. He resists, then can't. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into unease as he realizes someone expected him to come.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Flowers
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. In Hollowmere's church archives he finds decades of funeral records where flower orders encode names and dates — a ledger hidden in plain sight. The pattern points to a second death never investigated. Emotional beat: obsession kindling; the cold case becomes personal.

chapters.title: What the Widow Kept
chapters.summary: Widow Ada Fenwick, POV. Ada recalls the summer of 1984, her husband's silences, and the young woman who tended the graves of both victim and killer. She gives Orsen one clue and one warning. Emotional beat: grief braided with complicity; the past pressing on the present.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. He traces the letter to Marigold Ashcombe, the confessor's daughter, recently deceased herself — her obituary lists no survivors, but the ledger says otherwise. Emotional beat: the investigator confronting a mirror image: someone who died carrying an unsolved case.

chapters.title: Love Against the Vestry
chapters.summary: Marigold, POV (flashback). 1990s: Marigold falls for Thomas Hollowmere, heir to the family her father destroyed, and hides her father's crime to protect their fragile belonging. Emotional beat: tender, doomed love; duty devouring honesty.

chapters.title: A Case That Won't Close
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. His podcast episode flushes out threats from Hollowmere descendants who want the ledger burned. Someone ransacks the church archive. Emotional beat: rising dread; Orsen realizes he's inside the story now, not narrating it.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Ada Fenwick, POV. Ada confesses she helped bury the truth: the second ledger name was her own son, drowned for what he witnessed. Her guilt explains the funeral timing — she waited until her death could unseal it. Emotional beat: devastating release after forty years of silence.

chapters.title: Marigold's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. In Marigold's hospice letters he finds the full decoded ledger and her plea: tell the truth, but let Thomas's grandchildren keep their name. Duty to the dead collides with mercy for the living. Emotional beat: moral crisis at the story's peak pressure point.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV, climax. At the Hollowmere estate, confronted by the family who'd rather bury the ledger than be buried by it, Orsen airs the final episode live: the confession, the cover-up, and Marigold's voice reading her last entry. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure; love against duty resolved in public truth.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV, resolution. Weeks later, Orsen returns to Hollowmere for the memorial the town finally holds for all its dead. Ada's son gets a headstone; Thomas's heirs, stripped of myth but not each other, thank him. Orsen, an outsider all his life, is asked to stay. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging; the coldest case closed warm.
